transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-16
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Ava Kim (Redwood CSM), Liam Chen (BrightCart Head of ML), Priya Rao (BrightCart Platform), Marcus Bell (BrightCart CTO)

Summary: weekly POC sync focused on finalizing model selection and version pinning strategy. Reviewed recent benchmark results, discussed cost vs latency tradeoffs, rollbacks and fallback behavior, and clarified security/questions for private deployment.

Topics: model selection, quantization, pinning vs auto-updates, rollbacks/fallbacks, Dedicated routing, SOC2/KMS/SSO, next steps + benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate squeezing this in. quick agenda: go over the results from last week's runs, talk model selection and pinning strategy, then actions.
[00:22] Liam: yeah thanks, we saw the sample throughput numbers, a few anomalies on the tail latencies on 8k sequences.
[00:35] Diego: right, so we re-ran with the quantized 8-bit build and observed median token latency down ~22% but p95 spiked on a pattern when KV cache warmed, i think that's where your anomalies are.
[00:50] Priya: when you say "quantized 8-bit build" is that the int8 dynamic path? sometimes those names get mixed up in our notes.
[01:05] Diego: yeah it's the 8-bit quant path, dynamic kernel selection. there might be a mismatch on long-token kernels that causes a regressive spike, we suspected the kernel selection table didn't pick the fused attention for that shape.
[01:25] Marcus: ok so operationally, what's our risk if we pin to that version? we don't want to push something that causes tail latency for checkout flows.
[01:38] Samira: good question — typical approach is: pin to the variant that gives you consistent median and acceptable p95, and enable a fallback route to a slightly heavier but stable fp16 variant for any request that breaches SLO.
[01:55] Liam: can you do a quick recap of how fallbacks work? I heard about routing policies before but want to make sure it's automatic.
[02:08] Diego: yes you can configure routing rules: e.g., primary route to quant-8bit-v1, if p95 > 500ms or model returns error code, auto-fallback to fp16-stable-v3. it's policy driven, and we also support region-based fallbacks and capacity-tier fallbacks.
[02:28] Liam: does the fallback preserve context? like does it keep KV cache?
[02:35] Diego: good catch — no, fallback to a different model variant will not preserve the in-memory KV cache from the original instance. we handle soft-fallbacks by rehydrating prefix caches where possible, but there can be a hit. we recommend canarying fallbacks on low-risk routes first.
[02:58] Priya: for our checkout latency SLO of 400ms p95, that cache rehydration hit could be problematic.
[03:10] Ava: totally noted. maybe we need a two-phase plan: pin subset of routes (non-checkout) to aggressive quant, and keep checkout pinned to fp16-stable until benching is clean.
[03:24] Marcus: and what about rollback? if quant-8bit-v1 is deployed and we see degradation, how fast can we rollback?
[03:34] Diego: rollbacks are instant from the control plane — you can force traffic to an earlier pinned version. there's a short window for in-flight requests finishing, but control-plane switch is immediate; our recommendation is to have automatic rollback triggers based on error rate or latency thresholds.
[03:51] Liam: okay that helps. we ran some token-cost estimates and the quant variant saves us around 30% token cost on inference compute, which is big if we scale.
[04:04] Samira: exactly — that's the tradeoff. cost vs tail latency and reliability. for BrightCart, suggested strategy: model selection matrix per route. e.g., chat + marketing routes -> quant-8bit; checkout -> fp16-stable; search/rerank -> mixed depending on QPS.
[04:23] Priya: we also need to cover security/compliance questions before we can spin dedicated or private. SOC 2, KMS, audit logs — we need those artifacts.
[04:35] Ava: we have SOC 2 Type II, we can share the compliance pack; KMS integration is supported (AWS KMS / customer-managed keys), and audit logs are available via the Console with retention options. I'll attach the pack after the call.
[04:52] Priya: great. also SSO? SAML.
[04:56] Samira: yes SAML/SSO is supported, RBAC roles can be mapped to your IdP.
[05:05] Liam: on the bench results you sent, some of the labels in the csv look off — model names were truncated and "redwood-dedicated" showed up as "red-ded" in a couple places, so our scripts failed to map them. small but annoying.
[05:20] Diego: ack, that's a transcription/naming mismatch on our side — we'll standardize model IDs in the sheet.
[05:30] Marcus: let's talk about the pinning window: once we pin a model version, can Redwood auto-update it for security patches or minor perf updates?
[05:41] Samira: pinning means you control the version — we won't auto-upgrade without your opt-in. we do push security patches for infra but model binaries remain pinned until you choose to promote. you can configure auto-promote for minor patch levels if you want.
[05:58] Priya: and in Private deployment (VPC/on-prem), how does model versioning work with our image registry?
[06:08] Diego: in Private, you can either let Redwood host the model artifacts in a customer-specific bucket or you can pull from your registry. the control plane records the exact model checksum, so rollbacks are still deterministic.
[06:23] Liam: any differences in fallback behavior on Private vs Hosted?
[06:28] Diego: conceptually similar, but the automated regional fallback depends on your private capacity. if you don't have cross-region capacity, fallback options are limited to the variants you host.
[06:42] Marcus: we want to run a 24-hour soak on the quant-8bit-v1 traffic pattern to see long tail effects. can Redwood run that in your infra or do we need to provision Dedicated?
[06:55] Samira: we can run that in Hosted on a reserved workload for the POC, we just need your sample prompts and traffic profile. if you want to replicate your exact infra networking, Dedicated or Private runs are better but not necessary for initial benching.
[07:12] Priya: ok we'll provide the profile. one more thing: model catalog naming — we want stable canonical names.
[07:20] Diego: noted. we'll use canonical names like: redwood/quant-8bit-v1@2026-02-10 and redwood/fp16-stable-v3@2026-01-18 so your scripts can parse.
[07:34] Liam: about monitoring — can we export per-route token cost and per-request trace ids?
[07:41] Ava: yes, Console provides token-level breakdown and trace ids. you can stream traces to your observability workspace or download CSVs.
[07:52] Marcus: what's the plan for regression alerts? we don't want a silent perf regression after a model swap.
[07:59] Samira: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitors tied to prompt sets. you can define thresholds and get regression alerts for model outputs or latency. we'll set that up for your critical prompts in the POC.
[08:13] Priya: do you recommend pinning by route or by model globally?
[08:18] Diego: route-level pinning is more flexible — it maps to business-critical flows. global pinning is simpler but riskier.
[08:26] Liam: let's walk through a concrete example — checkout flow pinned to fp16-stable-v3, marketing pinned to quant-8bit-v1, and both have fallback to fp16-stable-v3. is that sane?
[08:37] Samira: yes that's a good starting point. for marketing you can be more aggressive with quant. for checkout, keep the more stable variant.
[08:45] Marcus: what about traffic splitting for canaries? we want 1% initially then ramp.
[08:51] Diego: control plane supports gradual canary ramping, can do 1% -> 5% -> 25% etc, and automatic rollback on thresholds.
[09:00] Liam: can we tie rollback to both latency and objective QA metric? like if QA F1 drops 3% then rollback?
[09:08] Diego: yes you can configure composite triggers including output-quality regressions from Redwood Optimize.
[09:15] Priya: are there any known compatibility issues with our model family? we use a custom fine-tuned Llama-derivative.
[09:24] Diego: generally supported; small differences in tokenizer and custom embeddings can matter. if it's a custom fine-tune, we recommend bringing the tokenizer and running a compatibility pass.
[09:36] Liam: ok. on the bench results you ran last week, can you summarize the p95s for each variant?
[09:43] Diego: sure — quant-8bit-v1 median ~ 38ms per token, p95 ~ 620ms on 8k sequences; fp16-stable-v3 median ~ 48ms, p95 ~ 420ms. those numbers vary by sequence length and batch size.
[10:02] Samira: so tradeoff is cost savings vs p95.
[10:06] Marcus: is that p95 consistent across regions?
[10:10] Diego: it's slightly better in our eu-west region in these runs because of GPU topology, but not significant. we'll include regional breakdown in the bench results.
[10:22] Liam: what about continuous batching — will that change p95?
[10:27] Diego: continuous batching helps throughput but can add latency variance for low QPS routes; for checkout we recommend reserved capacity with strict batching policies.
[10:39] Priya: can Redwood Dedicated provide burst capacity for Black Friday-like spikes?
[10:45] Samira: yes Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with burst pools; it's part of the Dedicated offering and you can define burst caps.
[10:56] Marcus: any blockers left for us to start the 24-hour soak?
[11:01] Samira: we need the anonymized prompts, confirmation of SSO and network egress constraints, and we'll schedule the bench window.
[11:10] Priya: I'm flagged to get legal/ procurement sign-off for data handling, do you have a data processing addendum?
[11:18] Ava: yes we'll send the DPA and SOC 2 pack after call.
[11:24] Liam: final quick question — if the quant-8bit variant has a silent failure mode causing hallucinations occasionally, can we detect that automatically?
[11:33] Diego: Redwood Optimize can run eval suites and quality monitors against your prompt set and raise alerts; we'll set thresholds so you can auto-rollback if QA drops.
[11:44] Samira: ok let's recap actions...
[11:47] Samira: Redwood will run the 24-hour soak on quant-8bit-v1 in Hosted, Diego to run bench with 8k context and share logs by 2/18, Samira to share updated pricing and normalized model IDs, Ava to share SOC2 & DPA, BrightCart to provide prompt set and confirm network constraints.
[12:08] Liam: that's accurate. thanks everyone.
[12:12] Marcus: thanks, talk soon.
[12:15] End of meeting

Notes on transcript quality: some model names in bench CSVs were abbreviated; minor transcription/capture artifacts possible.
